newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Ex-emperor of Central African Republic in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Ex-emperor of Central African Republic in hospital.

text.p: The former self-styled emperor of the Central African Republic, Jean-Bedel Bokassa, has been admitted to hospital with kidney problems, hospital sources said on Wednesday.

Bokassa, 75, was admitted a week ago to the Hopital de l'Amitie in the capital Bangui but although his condition had improved slightly he was likely to be transferred to a more specialised clinic, they added.
Bokassa seized power in 1966. He crowned himself emperor in a lavish ceremony in 1977, only to be ousted in a French-backed coup in 1979.

Returning from exile in 1986, he was sentenced to death for murder and embezzlement after a trial during which he was accused of cannibalism and infanticide. The then military leader Andre Kolingba commuted the sentence to life in jail, then to 20 years and then 10 years.
After his release by Kolingba in 1993, Bokassa said he would return to power if public opinion supported him. The government banned him for life from elections.

He has since lived quietly in Bangui but in July he announced that he had asked President Ange-Felix Patasse for an amnesty so that he could stand as a candidate in presidential elections planned for 1999.
